diagnosis_plain: Non-obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM) — ACVIM Stage B1

pet.chief_complaint: Grade II heart murmur detected at annual exam; occasional mild rapid breathing
pet.history: No prior cardiac history; routine annual exam

summary.severity: Moderate concern — structural changes present, no symptoms yet
summary.prognosis: Favorable at current stage; median survival >5 years for Stage B1
summary.paths: 2 paths: Medical therapy (Atenolol) vs. Watchful waiting
summary.priority_match: Watchful waiting aligns with owner's preference to minimize stress
summary.next_step: Recheck echocardiogram in 6 months; monitor resting respiratory rate daily

findings.name: Interventricular Septum (IVSd)
findings.meaning: Thickened — primary diagnostic criterion for HCM

findings.name: Left Atrium / Aorta Ratio (LA/Ao)
findings.meaning: Mildly elevated — left atrium beginning to enlarge

findings.name: SAM (Systolic Anterior Motion)
findings.meaning: No outflow obstruction; beta-blockers not indicated

paths.label: Option A
paths.survival: Helps manage symptoms; no proven survival benefit at Stage B1
paths.aligns: Suitable for LA/Ao ≥1.5 with clinical symptoms; proactive owners
paths.tensions: Hypotension, bradycardia risk; requires dose titration; adds stress for anxious cats

paths.label: Option B
paths.survival: No evidence of harm; median survival >5 years at Stage B1
paths.aligns: ACVIM consensus for asymptomatic B1; reduces vet visits; aligns with owner's stress-minimization priority
paths.tensions: Risk of missing early progression if monitoring is inconsistent

prognosis_bullets: Asymptomatic HCM (Stage B1/B2): Median survival exceeds 5 years; many cats never progress to heart failure
Congestive heart failure (Stage C): Median survival ~6–18 months; requires urgent hospitalization and long-term diuretics
Aortic thromboembolism (ATE): Occurs in ~12–17% of HCM cats; one of the most dangerous complications
Key factors: rate of left atrial enlargement, ATE occurrence, and consistency of monitoring
prognosis_note: Mochi was caught at a relatively early stage — regular follow-up is the single most important intervention right now. The LA/Ao of 1.52 warrants close attention at the next recheck.
questions: Given the LA/Ao of 1.52, do you recommend starting clopidogrel for thromboprophylaxis?
Should we add an NT-proBNP blood test to the monitoring plan?
How soon should the next recheck be? Is it important to use the same echocardiography machine for consistent measurements?
If I notice increased resting respiratory rate at home (>30 breaths/minute), should I go to an emergency clinic immediately?
HCM has a genetic component — should I have any littermates screened?
What everyday stressors should we minimize? (e.g., bathing, long-distance travel)
sources: ACVIM Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease in Dogs (2019)
Ferasin L. Feline myocardial disease. J Feline Med Surg. 2012
Payne JR et al. Prognostic indicators in cats with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. J Vet Intern Med. 2013
